intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that osteogenesis imperfecta type X (OI10) is caused by homozygous mutation in the SERPINH1 gene (600943) on chromosome 11q13.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type X (OI10) is caused by homozygous mutation in the SERPINH1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity for a missense mutation in SERPINH1, which encodes the collagen chaperone protein HSP47, results in severe recessive osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.explanation: The title says homozygous SERPINH1 mutation causes severe recessive OI. The 'OI10' label is OMIM nomenclature.

checks.claim: The SERPINH1 gene is located on chromosome 11q13.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified an autosomal-recessive missense mutation (c.233T>C, p.Leu78Pro) in SERPINH1
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosomal location (11q13). Because this is standard gene nomenclature restating the gene, it is accepted.

paragraphs.text: Osteogenesis imperfecta type X is a severe autosomal recessive form of osteogenesis imperfecta, a connective tissue disorder marked by bone fragility. Patients have multiple fractures and bone deformities. The disorder is caused by defects in HSP47, an endoplasmic reticulum chaperone that binds procollagen.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type X is a severe form of osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.evidence_quote: that leads to a severe OI phenotype
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the phenotype as severe.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type X is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified an autosomal-recessive missense mutation (c.233T>C, p.Leu78Pro) in SERPINH1
checks.explanation: The abstract calls the mutation autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta is a connective tissue disorder marked by bone fragility.
checks.evidence_quote: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is characterized by bone fragility and fractures
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions bone fragility but does not call OI a connective tissue disorder.

checks.claim: Patients with osteogenesis imperfecta type X have multiple fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is characterized by bone fragility and fractures that may be accompanied by bone deformity
checks.explanation: Fractures are described for OI in general. The abstract does not say this patient had multiple fractures.

checks.claim: Patients with osteogenesis imperfecta type X have bone deformities.
checks.evidence_quote: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is characterized by bone fragility and fractures that may be accompanied by bone deformity
checks.explanation: Bone deformity is described for OI in general, not specifically for the SERPINH1 patient.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type X is caused by defects in HSP47.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity for a missense mutation in SERPINH1, which encodes the collagen chaperone protein HSP47, results in severe recessive osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.explanation: The title links HSP47 defects to the disease.

checks.claim: HSP47 is an endoplasmic reticulum chaperone that binds procollagen.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation results in degradation of the endoplasmic reticulum resident HSP47 via the proteasome.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls HSP47 an ER-resident collagen chaperone but does not explicitly say it binds procollagen.

paragraphs.text: Christiansen et al. (2010) reported a child of Saudi Arabian origin with severe osteogenesis imperfecta. Features included multiple fractures, bone deformities, blue sclerae, and dentinogenesis imperfecta. The child also had renal stones.

checks.claim: Christiansen et al. (2010) reported a child with severe osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.evidence_quote: that leads to a severe OI phenotype
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a single affected individual with severe OI but does not say the individual was a child.

checks.claim: The child with severe osteogenesis imperfecta reported by Christiansen et al. (2010) was of Saudi Arabian origin.
checks.explanation: The patient's ethnic origin is not stated in the abstract (only the abstract was supplied).

checks.claim: The child reported by Christiansen et al. (2010) had multiple fractures.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not describe the patient's clinical features (only the abstract was supplied).

checks.claim: The child reported by Christiansen et al. (2010) had bone deformities.
checks.explanation: The patient's bone deformities are not described in the abstract (only the abstract was supplied).

checks.claim: The child reported by Christiansen et al. (2010) had blue sclerae.
checks.explanation: Blue sclerae are not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: The child reported by Christiansen et al. (2010) had dentinogenesis imperfecta.
checks.explanation: Dentinogenesis imperfecta is mentioned only as a general OI feature, not as a feature of this patient.

checks.claim: The child reported by Christiansen et al. (2010) had renal stones.
checks.explanation: Renal stones are not mentioned in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Christiansen et al. (2010) found homozygous mutation in their patient, which indicates autosomal recessive inheritance of OI10.

checks.claim: Christiansen et al. (2010) found a homozygous mutation in their patient with OI10.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity for a missense mutation in SERPINH1
checks.explanation: The title states the patient was homozygous.

checks.claim: The homozygous mutation in the patient of Christiansen et al. (2010) indicates autosomal recessive inheritance of OI10.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified an autosomal-recessive missense mutation (c.233T>C, p.Leu78Pro) in SERPINH1
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the mutation as autosomal recessive.

paragraphs.text: In a child with severe osteogenesis imperfecta, Christiansen et al. (2010) found a homozygous missense mutation in the SERPINH1 gene, leu78-to-pro (L78P). The candidate gene approach was prompted by the earlier finding of SERPINH1 mutation in Dachshunds with OI (Drogemuller et al., 2009). In the patient's cells, the mutant HSP47 protein was unstable and degraded by the proteasome. Type I procollagen processing and secretion were abnormal.

checks.claim: Christiansen et al. (2010) found a homozygous missense mutation in the SERPINH1 gene in a child with severe osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity for a missense mutation in SERPINH1, which encodes the collagen chaperone protein HSP47, results in severe recessive osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.explanation: Homozygous missense mutation with severe OI matches. The 'child' detail is not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: The SERPINH1 mutation found by Christiansen et al. (2010) is leu78-to-pro (L78P).
checks.evidence_quote: missense mutation (c.233T>C, p.Leu78Pro) in SERPINH1
checks.explanation: p.Leu78Pro is the same variant as L78P.

checks.claim: Christiansen et al. (2010) used a candidate gene approach for SERPINH1 prompted by the earlier finding of SERPINH1 mutation in Dachshunds with osteogenesis imperfecta (Drogemuller et al., 2009).
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention a candidate gene approach or the Dachshund findings.

checks.claim: In cells from the patient of Christiansen et al. (2010), the mutant L78P HSP47 protein was unstable.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation results in degradation of the endoplasmic reticulum resident HSP47 via the proteasome.
checks.explanation: Degradation of the mutant protein implies it is unstable.

checks.claim: In cells from the patient of Christiansen et al. (2010), the mutant L78P HSP47 protein was degraded by the proteasome.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation results in degradation of the endoplasmic reticulum resident HSP47 via the proteasome.
checks.explanation: The abstract states proteasomal degradation directly.

checks.claim: In cells from the patient of Christiansen et al. (2010), type I procollagen processing was abnormal.
checks.evidence_quote: Type I procollagen accumulates in the Golgi of fibroblasts from the affected individual and a population of the secreted type I procollagen is protease sensitive.
checks.explanation: Procollagen accumulating in the Golgi and protease sensitivity indicate abnormal processing.

checks.claim: In cells from the patient of Christiansen et al. (2010), type I procollagen secretion was abnormal.
checks.evidence_quote: a population of the secreted type I procollagen is protease sensitive. These findings suggest that HSP47 monitors the integrity of the triple helix of type I procollagen at the ER/cis-Golgi boundary and, when absent, the rate of transit from the ER to the Golgi is increased
checks.explanation: The secreted procollagen is abnormal (protease sensitive) and ER-to-Golgi transit is altered. The abstract does not explicitly say secretion itself was abnormal.

paragraphs.text: Drogemuller et al. (2009) studied Dachshunds with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta and found a homozygous missense mutation in the canine SERPINH1 gene, leu326-to-pro (L326P).

checks.claim: Drogemuller et al. (2009) studied Dachshunds with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention Dachshunds or Drogemuller et al.

checks.claim: Drogemuller et al. (2009) found a homozygous missense mutation in the canine SERPINH1 gene in Dachshunds with osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention the canine SERPINH1 mutation.

checks.claim: The canine SERPINH1 mutation found by Drogemuller et al. (2009) in Dachshunds is leu326-to-pro (L326P).
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The canine L326P mutation is not mentioned in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Nagai et al. (2000) found that mice lacking Hsp47 died during embryonic development and had abnormal collagen formation.

checks.claim: Nagai et al. (2000) found that mice lacking Hsp47 died during embryonic development.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention Hsp47 knockout mice or Nagai et al.

checks.claim: Nagai et al. (2000) found that mice lacking Hsp47 had abnormal collagen formation.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention Hsp47 knockout mice.

paragraphs.text: In a child of Saudi Arabian origin with severe osteogenesis imperfecta type X, Christiansen et al. (2010) found a homozygous leu78-to-pro (L78P) mutation in the SERPINH1 gene. The mutant protein was unstable and degraded by the proteasome, and procollagen processing was abnormal.

checks.claim: Christiansen et al. (2010) found a homozygous leu78-to-pro (L78P) mutation in the SERPINH1 gene in a child with severe osteogenesis imperfecta type X.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity for a missense mutation in SERPINH1, which encodes the collagen chaperone protein HSP47, results in severe recessive osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.explanation: The title and abstract (p.Leu78Pro) support a homozygous L78P mutation with severe OI.

checks.claim: The child with the homozygous SERPINH1 L78P mutation reported by Christiansen et al. (2010) was of Saudi Arabian origin.
checks.explanation: The patient's Saudi Arabian origin is not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: The mutant SERPINH1 L78P protein was unstable.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation results in degradation of the endoplasmic reticulum resident HSP47 via the proteasome.
checks.explanation: Degradation of the mutant protein implies it is unstable.

checks.claim: The mutant SERPINH1 L78P protein was degraded by the proteasome.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation results in degradation of the endoplasmic reticulum resident HSP47 via the proteasome.
checks.explanation: The abstract states proteasomal degradation directly.

checks.claim: Procollagen processing was abnormal in the presence of the SERPINH1 L78P mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Type I procollagen accumulates in the Golgi of fibroblasts from the affected individual and a population of the secreted type I procollagen is protease sensitive.
checks.explanation: These findings show abnormal procollagen processing.
